summary: On August 12, 2026 the IRS released Notice 2026-49, proposing sample forms and standardized procedures for rollovers between employer retirement plans and IRAs under SECURE 2.0 Section 324 (IRA-to-IRA transfers aren't covered). source: Analysis of employer pay stub + Truthifi transaction history
summary: Employee 401(k) elective deferrals are on pace to reach the annual IRS limit within the next 1-2 pay periods — well ahead of year-end — driven partly by a variable annual bonus (paid quarterly) that also has 401(k) withheld. Reaching the cap early causes employee deferrals to stop for the rest of the year. If the plan's employer Safe Harbor match is calculated per-pay-period rather than trued-up annually, this is a well-documented 401(k) mechanics pitfall: stopping contributions early can forfeit employer match for every remaining pay period of the year.
suggestedAction: Confirm with HR or the plan administrator (via the Summary Plan Description) whether the Safe Harbor match includes an annual true-up provision. If yes, no action needed — the employer will true up the match after year-end. If no, consider reducing the per-paycheck contribution percentage next year so contributions spread evenly across all pay periods instead of maxing out early.
